How inspection citations work
  • Source: CMS Nursing Home Health Citations.
  • Survey date → PDF: Valid dates link to the Medicare Care Compare inspection PDF. Otherwise the cell shows why the PDF link is unavailable.
  • Scope/Severity (A–L): CMS encodes scope and resident harm in one letter per deficiency (A = lowest, L = highest). The table sorts by that letter (A through L). Severe only (G and above) filters to the high-harm band; red shading highlights H and above.
  • Row color: Amber highlights the G+ dashboard citation-flag band. Red highlights H and above (stricter subset). Severe only (G and above) limits the table to that G+ band.
  • Survey quarters: Deficiency rows roll up by the inspection survey date calendar quarter. That label may not match this facility’s PBJ work-date quarter or CMS Provider Information processing quarter for the same period.
  • Topic chips: When the staffing context card is shown, click a topic (Abuse/neglect, Care planning, etc.) to filter this table. Severe (G+) syncs with the severe-only checkbox.

Citation context (staffing-linked)

Staffing-linked citations only — survey-date context, not proof of causation. PBJ day links apply only when exact incident dates are verified.

State minimum staffing — summary count
  • What is counted: Days in the active filter with a possible staffing flag — either {{ compliance_state_long }} total nurse HPRD reported below the state benchmark and/or total RN hours below 8 (federal RN presence PBJ proxy; total RN, not direct-care RN).
  • Denominator: Days with zero census are excluded from both the below-standard count and the total-day count (same rule as the Compliance section).
  • Threshold source: State minimum HPRD is loaded from the PBJ320 state staffing reference (MACPAC / state policy). The label shows the rounded threshold and state abbreviation (for example, < 2.56 NJ Min).
  • Full compliance tools: Use the Analyze staffing compliance bar in Staffing for charts, below-standard day tables, and editable thresholds. Use View PBJ Compliance to open the review memo with charts, below-standard day tables, and editable thresholds. CMS star ratings are under Census & occupancy detail. Jump to compliance tools{% if state_standard_info and state_standard_info.state_code_citation %} · {{ compliance_state_long }} regulation link{% endif %}.
CMS Staffing Rating

The star shown in PBJ Trends is the simple average of CMS staffing ratings for each matched provider quarter in your filter (1–5 stars in half-star steps). Single-quarter filters use that quarter’s rating; multi-quarter filters average all quarters with a rating in the span. Ratings update on CMS processing quarters, not PBJ work dates.

CMS Staffing Rating — Six PBJ-based measures: three case-mix-adjusted nurse HPRD levels (one quarter) and three staff-turnover rates (six consecutive PBJ quarters), using MDS census.

Related CMS domains: Overall adjusts from health inspection ± staffing and quality; health inspection reflects survey deficiencies; quality measures cover 15 clinical QMs.

Source: CMS Five-Star Users Guide (PDF)

PBJ staffing standards review · {{ compliance_state_long }}

Two independent categories: federal staffing proxies (PBJ daily-hour flags under federal law) and state standard / benchmark (this facility’s {{ compliance_state_long }} reference). Federal proxies do not replace or override state benchmarks.

Federal staffing proxies
  • RN presence (default): 8+ total RN hours/day uses total RN hours (direct + admin + DON) — not direct-care RN only. PBJ proxy under 42 CFR § 483.35. Daily totals do not prove consecutive RN hours; waivers are not reflected. Direct RN is a contextual warning only.
  • Licensed-nurse hours: 24+ total RN + total LPN/LVN hours/day sums reported licensed-nurse hours per calendar day under 42 CFR § 483.35(a)(1). Daily totals do not prove continuous 24-hour staffing; waivers are not reflected.
  • Federal results are possible staffing flags or reported below threshold (PBJ proxy) — not definitive compliance findings.
State standard / benchmark · {{ compliance_state_long }}
  • Threshold: Editable {{ compliance_state_long }} HPRD benchmark from MACPAC-style reference{% if state_standard_info and state_standard_info.state_code_citation %} (state rule){% endif %}.
  • Comparison: Total or direct nursing HPRD vs. that benchmark — separate from federal proxies.
  • Denominator: Days with zero census are excluded from day counts.
Day tools & sources
  • Below-threshold days: Daily row, PBJ320 Report, and Roster shortcuts on each flagged day.
  • Breakdowns: Weekday/month summaries use below-threshold days only for the active filter.
  • Dashboard methodology · MACPAC. Verify current regulatory text before legal use.

Staffing benchmarks — methodology

How CMS quarters line up and what each benchmark series means.

Quarter matching

Provider Information processing dates and PBJ work quarters are aligned using CMS collection windows and day-level staffing overlap so reported, case-mix, and adjusted series share the same quarter labels as the rest of this report. Step-by-step rules: quarter matching.

Series on the charts
  • Reported — facility-reported nursing HPRD from Provider Information for the matched quarter.
  • Case-mix — CMS case-mix nurse staffing hours per resident day for that quarter (Provider Information / PBJ documentation). This is not a separate non-CMS “clinical expectation”; it is the published case-mix staffing series tied to PDPM nursing case-mix and national reported-hour means.
  • Adjusted — CMS adjusted staffing HPRD where published on the same Provider Information row.
CMS definitions (nursing case-mix hours & CMI)

CMS describes how facility nursing case-mix index (CMI) and case-mix HPRD are built from MDS-assigned PDPM nursing CMGs, resident-days, a national weighted-average CMI, a facility relative CMI ratio, and the formula case-mix HPRD = facility CMI ratio × national mean of reported HPRD (with separate calculations for RN vs all nursing and for weekends where published). The same PBJ Users Guide explains historical rules (for example, facilities with total nurse staffing under 1.5 HPRD were excluded before January 2022) and that the label “case-mix hours” replaced the older term “expected hours” after April 2019.

Primary source (PDF): CMS Payroll-Based Journal / Provider Information Users Guide.

Related CMS references: PDPM (SNF PPS); nursing CMI weights and policy context in the FY 2024 SNF PPS final rule (Federal Register). Further definitions: Methodology and sources on this page.

Harrington & other benchmarks

Elsewhere under Staffing Benchmarks, quarterly PBJ rollups and Harrington-style expected staffing use the same facility timeline. Harrington rows need a non-null nursing case-mix index from Provider Information for that quarter; when CMS does not publish that index for a row, the CMI column shows “—” even if case-mix HPRD is present.

Star ratings and quality measures can refresh on a different CMS cadence than staffing HPRD; the ratings-over-time chart follows Provider Information as released per row.

Red flag history

PBJ320 flags are a composite from CMS Provider Information (SFF status, star ratings, abuse icon, ownership, administrator turnover, etc.), matched to PBJ quarters. Matched-quarter methodology.

Suggested events appear at the top of the Events section. Flag history lists individual flags by date and quarter. Click a row or Details for what it means and shortcuts (rating trends, citations, before/after windows, filter to quarter). Use Source in the detail modal for the underlying CMS file.

When G+ citations appear, they are merged from the local NH Health Citations extract for counsel visibility — not a Provider Information field. Deficiency letters (A–L), severe filters, and shading are documented under Inspections & deficiencies.

  • 1-Star Staffing / Overall — CMS star domains; open rating trends chart.
  • SFF / SFF Candidate — Special Focus Facility program status from Provider Information.
  • Admin TO — Facility-level administrator turnover count from Provider Information (not an Employee Detail ID).
  • Ownership — Provider changed ownership in last 12 months; can anchor the Before vs after tool.
  • Abuse icon — CMS abuse icon on Care Compare; citation context when loaded.
  • G+ citations — Severe deficiency band from NH Health Citations extract.

Outliers

Period screening flags days where daily PBJ is unusual vs the mean of the period you select (active filter or all history). Threshold: |Z| ≥ 2.

Day report (single work date) uses separate baselines — calendar year, fiscal quarter, and weekday — so one day can look normal in one view and flagged in the other. Both are intentional.

Peer & regional comparison

County = census-weighted mean HPRD across nursing homes in this facility’s county (same state), from CMS-published facility-quarter rollups. State, CMS region, and National use CMS PBJ quarterly staffing series for the selected period.

Match rural/urban peers limits state, region, and county columns to the same CMS urban/rural designation as this facility (Provider Information), so comparisons stay within the same peer type.

The facility column uses filtered daily PBJ for the active date range; geography columns use CMS quarterly rollups for the selected period (not the custom day filter).

Dashboard sections: PBJ Nursing Home Staffing Intelligence (profile, trends, compliance tools, census detail, ratings) → Acuity & Regional Benchmarks → Patterns → Events → Daily Staffing & Roster Review. Top nav Compliance scrolls to the staffing compliance block; Forensics opens the day-level roster review. Case Builder and Methodology are linked from the nav.

Primary source links appear under each heading below.

Staff Categories
  • Total Staff: All nursing staff including RNs, LPNs, CNAs, RN/LPN administrators, and DON
  • Direct Staff: Staff providing direct patient care (excludes administrators and DON)
  • Total RN (Registered Nurse): Includes RNs + RN administrators + RN DON (Director of Nursing)
  • Direct RN: Excludes RN Admin, RN DON.
  • LPN (Licensed Practical Nurse): Includes direct care LPNs + LPN administrators
  • Nurse Aides: Includes CNAs + NA trainees + Medication Aides
  • Contract Staff: Temporary/agency staff (marked with "_ctr" suffix)
  • Case-mix: CMS acuity benchmark from Provider Information (reported HPRD ÷ expected)
Calculations
  • HPRD (Hours Per Resident Day): Total hours ÷ census for the same day or period.
  • Rounding: Half-up (ROUND_HALF_UP) for displayed values; CSV tooltips may restate rounded components for readability.
  • Non-Direct Staff: RN Admin/DON & LPN Admin hours per resident day
  • State peer rank (summary): When shown, “higher than X% of {state} facilities” compares this home to other nursing homes in the same state for the CMS-matched Provider Information quarter—a cross-sectional snapshot, not the custom date filter.
More calculations (contract %, case-mix %, EIN, shift bands)
  • Contract Staff %: Contract nursing hours divided by direct-care RN, LPN, and CNA line hours (Hrs_RN_ctr+Hrs_LPN_ctr+Hrs_CNA_ctr over Hrs_RN+Hrs_LPN+Hrs_CNA; excludes admin/DON, NA trainee, and medication aide) × 100.
  • Summary contract % (banner / /api/summary): Recomputed from summed contract hours and summed direct-care RN+LPN+CNA hours across the active filter—sum(Hrs_RN_ctr+Hrs_LPN_ctr+Hrs_CNA_ctr) ÷ sum(Hrs_RN+Hrs_LPN+Hrs_CNA) × 100—not averaged from daily percentages. Blank when the denominator sum is zero or missing.
  • Summary period HPRD (banner / API summary): Sum of staff hours ÷ sum of census across filtered days (resident-day weighting), not the simple mean of each day’s HPRD column.
  • Other summary fields: Mean census (etc.) are ordinary arithmetic means across days unless stated elsewhere in this section.
  • Shift-band projection (day report): CMS PBJ daily files do not include shift-level hours. For context only, the day report may show illustrative Day / Evening / Overnight splits by applying published national shift-distribution shares to that calendar day’s RN+LPN hour pool and nurse-aide hour pool (then dividing by census for HPRD). This is not a CMS-reported field. These splits are illustrative estimates from published national distribution shares—not the facility’s actual shift schedules—and should not be cited as proof of a shift-level staffing violation. Primary source: JAMDA (2024).
  • EIN roster — daily hour realism (CMS PBJ):
  • Employee Detail (EIN) extract and positions: Row-level files include all CMS EMPLEE_JOB_CD_ID values (1-34). The nursing roster view is intentionally narrower (Administrator 1 plus nursing 5-12) for direct PBJ comparability. Non-nurse analysis uses the same underlying EIN file and mapped non-nurse job codes (medical, therapy, activities, social services, support).
  • Dual role badge (EIN roster / employee modal): Shown when the same CMS employee ID appears with more than one distinct nursing job code (Administrator 1 or codes 5–12) anywhere in the loaded Employee Detail extract. Hover lists the roles held. Separate from the per-quarter New badge (first quarter for that employee–job pair in file).
  • % Case-Mix HPRD: (Reported HPRD ÷ CMS case-mix expected HPRD) × 100 — i.e. reported as a percent of the acuity-based staffing targets in Provider Information. Values below 100% indicate reported staffing below that CMS-reported benchmark for the quarter; above 100% indicate surplus. Methodology: Five-Star / Care Compare Technical Users’ Guide (PDF); broader QM & case-mix docs: Nursing Home Quality Initiatives. Dataset: Nursing Home Provider Information (4pq5-n9py).
Harrington Expected Staffing

Harrington et al. publish expected staffing as a function of CMS nursing case-mix index (CMI) from Provider Information. The quarterly table here includes CMI quarters from 2024 Q1 onward (newest first). Expected HPRD and percent-of-expected use full-precision CMI; displayed cells round for readability.

  • Total Expected HPRD:
    3.48 + [((CMI - 0.62) / (3.84 - 0.62))0.715 × (7.68 - 3.48)]
  • RN Expected HPRD:
    0.55 + [((CMI - 0.62) / (3.84 - 0.62))0.974 × (2.39 - 0.55)]
  • Nurse Aide Expected HPRD:
    2.45 + [((CMI - 0.62) / (3.84 - 0.62))0.236 × (3.6 - 2.45)]
  • LPN Expected HPRD: Total nurse expected − RN expected − Nurse aide expected (no separate Harrington formula; licensed nurse time was pooled in the source studies).
  • % of expected: 100 × (reported HPRD ÷ Harrington expected HPRD), rounded; follows the Harrington table’s Total vs Direct toggle (default Total): Total Staff HPRD (total row), Total RN HPRD (RN), Total Nurse Aide HPRD (nurse aide), Total LPN HPRD (LPN, compared to derived expected LPN). diff columns in CSV = reported − expected.

Primary citation: Nursing Home Guide to Adjusting Nurse Staffing for Resident Case-Mix (Harrington et al., Journal of the American Geriatrics Society).

Note: Direct Care metrics are calculated from PBJ and exclude Admin/DON.

CMS case-mix / Five-Star context: Care Compare / Five-Star Technical Users’ Guide (PDF) · Nursing Home Quality Initiatives (quality measures & case-mix documentation).

NH health citations & deficiencies
  • Source: CMS Nursing Home Health Citations (r5ix-sfxw). The deficiency table uses the facility’s CMS extract when present; open the same dataset on Data.CMS.gov (CCN pre-filtered when available).
  • Scope/Severity (A–L): CMS assigns one letter per deficiency combining scope and resident harm (A = lowest, L = highest). The table sorts by letter (A→L). Severe only limits rows to G and above; red row shading highlights H and above.
  • Survey timing: Deficiency timelines and “survey quarter” labels use the inspection survey date — not PBJ work-date quarters or Provider Information processing quarters.
  • Red Flag History: When present, G+ deficiency citations are merged into the facility red-flag narrative (counts and date span from flagged rows).

Non-nurse PBJ staffing
  • Source: CMS PBJ — Daily Non-Nurse Staffing.
  • HPRD & hours: Non-nurse hours follow CMS role columns in the Daily Non-Nurse Staffing file; HPRD-style values use sum of hours ÷ census where shown, consistent with nurse PBJ.
  • Deduping: Rows are deduplicated on WorkDate (and aligned keys) so daily totals and calendar coverage are not double-counted when CMS publishes overlapping extracts.
  • Signals: Leadership and coverage callouts flag sparse categories or all-zero non-nurse days relative to loaded quarters; see the non-nurse section headers for the exact thresholds.

Statistical Analysis
  • Z-Score: (Value - Mean) ÷ Standard Deviation
  • Outlier Detection: |Z-Score| ≥ 2.0 (High), |Z-Score| ≥ 3.0 (Extreme)
  • Percentile: Approximate ranking compared to historical data
  • Holidays: Federal holidays as defined by U.S. government
Numerical behavior & audit-oriented choices

Judgment calls and implementation details for litigation-grade use. Where the UI disagrees with a naïve mean, the behavior below is intentional.

  • Server pipeline (daily row file): Derived columns (e.g. total staff hours, total HPRD) may apply per-row rounding before storage. Filter-level summary HPRD still uses sum(hours) ÷ sum(census) on those columns, so it tracks CMS intent; tiny drift vs raw unpublished CMS sums is possible.
  • Summary contract %: Filter-level banner value uses sum(Hrs_RN_ctr+Hrs_LPN_ctr+Hrs_CNA_ctr) ÷ sum(Hrs_RN+Hrs_LPN+Hrs_CNA) × 100 on filtered daily rows—the same direct-care components as daily Total Contract %—not the mean of each day’s percentage.
  • Snapshot modal — PBJ Trends chart: Each daily point is that row’s total HPRD. Month / quarter / year buckets use sum(Total Staff Hours) ÷ sum(MDScensus) for days with census > 0 so the curve matches aggregate HPRD math; days with missing or non-positive census are left out of the bucket (conservative vs counting hours with no resident denominator).
  • Staffing trend — census context rail: Beside the nursing HPRD chart (desktop), a vertical summary shows avg census for the active filter (with sparkline) and occupancy from the same census series. On narrow screens it stacks under the chart. Occupancy uses Provider Information licensed capacity when available.
  • Census detail table — annual rows: Certified beds use the mean of quarterly Provider Information bed counts in that calendar year; occupancy % uses annual average census ÷ that mean (or the mean of quarterly occupancy % when available).
  • Acuity / CMS % Case-Mix (overview and snapshot): Uses all Provider Information quarters in the filter (averaged when multiple). Quarters without published case-mix are skipped; partial filter edges still use full-quarter CMS values.
  • Published geography — calendar year: Peer HPRD and related fields are the simple mean of CMS quarterly published values for that year—not a resident-day–weighted recomputation from daily PBJ unless CMS already defined the rollup that way.
  • Published geography — “This facility”: Same sum-hours ÷ sum-census rule as summary, but only days with census > 0 in the chosen quarter or calendar year (see geography card).
  • Geography period dropdown: Saved scope in browser storage is validated against the current filter’s min/max work dates; invalid years or quarters reset to Latest in filter. Empty daily data does not reuse a prior cached row set for geography or state-minimum counts.
  • State minimum caption (overview bullet): If no MACPAC-style state minimum is loaded for the facility, the bullet says so explicitly — a substitute federal number is not labeled as the state threshold.
  • Audit scope line (filters / watermark): If quarter or date-range APIs fail, the displayed span uses this page’s CMS work-date bounds when available; it does not fall back to a fixed invented year range.
  • Client display helpers: Functions such as roundHalfUpDisplay return formatted strings for UI and labels; core ratios in script use numeric API fields, not parsed display strings.

PBJ bucket → EIN code(s)
  • Hrs_RN → 7
  • Total RN → 5, 6, 7 · Hrs_RNadmin → 6 · Hrs_RNDON → 5
  • Hrs_LPN → 9 · Total LPN → 8, 9 · Hrs_LPNadmin → 8

Roster job codes (EMPLEE_JOB_CD_ID)
1 Administrator · 5 RN DON · 6 RN Admin · 7 RN · 8 LPN Admin · 9 LPN/LVN · 10 CNA · 11 aide in training · 12 med aide

Full EIN coverage (why not all positions listed here): The extract keeps all CMS job codes (1–34), but this quick legend intentionally shows the nursing-focused PBJ comparison set (1 and 5–12) to keep the row readable. Additional non-nurse positions are still included in the same EIN file and power the non-nurse roster/day views (therapy, social services, activities, dietary, housekeeping, maintenance, admin support, and other non-nurse roles).

Role position numbers (#1, #2, …): For each job code, employees are numbered in order of first work day in the loaded Employee Detail file for that role (then tie-break by employee ID). #1 = earliest first appearance for that code; several people each keep their own #. In All quarters roster view, rows are grouped person×role (employee-first), and Active means that person×role appears in the most recent quarter. Labels are for readability only. Not inspection citations: Deficiency tags, Form 2567 statement numbers, and similar citation labels come from a different CMS system and are unrelated to these roster numbers or job codes.

  • Headcount lens definitions (distinct employees): Distinct employee counts are tracked by bucket: all, admin, nursing total, nursing direct, nursing leadership, and non-nurse. Contract headcount is tracked separately (all contract, nurse contract, non-nurse contract; admin-contract where applicable). Buckets are de-duplicated within bucket/time window by employee ID, but overlap across buckets is expected, so counts are not additive.
  • Time grain: Day views show distinct employees for one work date; quarter views show distinct employees across the quarter, including contract splits where published. Buckets are available for all staff, nursing-only, non-nurse-only, direct nursing, and contract-focused slices.
  • PBJ bucket reconciliation scope: Comparisons use the same facility, same date, and mapped role codes (direct RN: 7; total RN: 5+6+7; total aide: 10+11+12). Differences usually reflect timing, role assignment, source granularity, or rounding, and are not by themselves proof of reporting error.
Cross-check in roster modal: PBJ daily column sum vs Employee Detail code-sum for that date. Warning threshold is ~±2.5 h or ~3%. Direct RN compares Hrs_RN vs code 7; total RN compares Hrs_RN + Hrs_RNadmin + Hrs_RNDON vs codes 5+6+7.
Headcount best practices: Use headcount with hours/HPRD (not alone), compare like-for-like role buckets, review day and quarter trends before conclusions, separate employee vs contract interpretations, and document job-code mapping plus date scope whenever citing PBJ↔EIN deltas.
Employee ID continuity review trigger (Headcount chart footer): Distinct SYS_EMPLEE_ID counts are a reported-roster / identifier-continuity measure, not a staffing-volume or census measure. The dashboard compares quarter-to-quarter ID changes against total hours, HPRD, hours per ID, workdays, position mix, and resident-days when available.
  • Base trigger: current-quarter unique IDs ≥ 1.5× prior quarter, or new-ID share ≥ 50%, or retention < 60%.
  • Major trigger: current-quarter unique IDs ≥ 2.0× prior quarter and new-ID share ≥ 60%.
  • Pattern labels (when triggered): possible high turnover/replacement staffing, roster fragmentation, ID remapping/reporting reset, staffing expansion, or generic continuity review — chosen from supporting hours/HPRD/position context, not ID counts alone.
Flags appear only as a compact, collapsed row under the Headcount chart when triggered. Expanded copy includes pattern, supporting metrics, CMS Employee Detail source-row links (prior and current quarter, filtered to this facility PROVNUM/CCN), and review prompts. Treat as a review trigger, not proof of turnover, bad data, fraud, or manipulation.

Harrington expected staffing — methodology

Expected staffing follows the published Harrington case-mix guide: each quarter’s nursing CMI (CMS Provider Information) becomes expected HPRD, then reported PBJ HPRD for the same quarter is compared as a percent of expected. Display rounding is half-up (“financial”) throughout this report.

Expected HPRD from CMI

Let r = (CMI − 0.62) / (3.84 − 0.62). Expected HPRD for each role is intercept + rexponent × (upper − intercept), with constants from Harrington et al.

  • Total nurse HPRD:
    3.48 + r0.715 × (7.68 − 3.48)
  • RN HPRD:
    0.55 + r0.974 × (2.39 − 0.55)
  • Nurse aide HPRD:
    2.45 + r0.236 × (3.6 − 2.45)
  • LPN HPRD (derived):
    Total nurse expected − RN expected − Nurse aide expectedHarrington time studies estimated licensed nurse (RN + LPN) together; there is no separate LPN curve.
% of expected

% of expected = ROUND_HALF_UP(100 × reported_hprd ÷ harrington_expected_hprd, 1)

The Acuity summary % Harrington Expected always uses total nurse HPRD in the numerator (not direct care). The quarterly table below can switch between total and direct HPRD for role-level detail.

In the Acuity summary card, the blue bar shows reported total nurse HPRD as a percent of Harrington expected (total basis). The badge turns orange below 100% and red below 75%.

When either value is missing or the denominator is zero, the cell shows N/A. CSV exports add diff (reported − expected) and work-shown strings for audit.

Reported HPRD (numerator)
  • Acuity summary %: PBJ total nurse HPRD only.
  • Quarterly table (toggle): Total = all role HPRD; Direct care = PBJ HPRD excluding RN Admin, RN DON, and LPN Admin.
  • LPN expected: Residual (total − RN − aide), not a separate published formula.
Quarters in the table

The quarterly table starts at 2024 Q1 (when nursing CMI is available for Harrington-style expected staffing in Provider Information). Earlier quarters are excluded.

After that cutoff, a row appears only when Provider Information publishes a positive nursing case-mix index for that quarter. Rows match the Case-Mix Acuity table for the same quarter.

Primary citation: Nursing Home Guide to Adjusting Nurse Staffing for Resident Case-Mix (Harrington et al., Journal of the American Geriatrics Society). CMS context: Care Compare / Five-Star Technical Users’ Guide (PDF) · Nursing Home Provider Information (4pq5-n9py).

Quarterly rollups — how to read

HPRD values show hours per resident day. Average hours per day for each role appear in parentheses when available.

Contract % uses contract RN+LPN+CNA hours in the numerator. Direct care divides by direct RN+LPN+CNA hours; total nurse divides by all nurse staff hours (includes admin/DON).

Bold cells mark quarter-over-quarter change of 20% or more: green = increase, red = decrease (vs. the prior quarter in this table).

Use Show all PBJ quarters to expand beyond the filter-focused window.

Case-Mix — how to read % CMS Case-Mix

% CMS Case-Mix is reported HPRD divided by CMS case-mix HPRD for the same quarter. 100% means reported hours match CMS case-mix; values below 100% mean less staffing than CMS case-mix for that role.

Total vs direct (two bases)
  • Total — all reported hours for the role (includes RN Admin, RN DON, LPN Admin where applicable). In the Acuity summary card, the amber/yellow bar shows this total-basis %.
  • Direct — direct care hours only (excludes those admin roles). In the Acuity summary card, the orange bar shows this direct-basis %.
Table cell tints (% columns)

Each Total or Direct column uses its own basis. Cell background reflects how far reported staffing is below CMS case-mix:

  • Red tint — below 80% of CMS case-mix
  • Yellow tint — 80% to under 95% of CMS case-mix
Acuity summary badge

The headline % uses the total basis. Orange badge = below 100%; red badge = below 75%.

CMS references: Five-Star technical guide (PDF) · NH quality & case-mix hub

Harrington table — how to read

Hover Expected for R and the role-specific Harrington line (half-up to 2 decimals). Hover % of exp. for 100 × reported ÷ expected (half-up to 1 decimal). The Acuity summary % Harrington Expected uses total nurse HPRD only. Blue row bands mark quarters in the active Summary & period filter after Apply.

R = (CMI − 0.62) / (3.84 − 0.62)
Total exp.: 3.48 + R0.715(7.68 − 3.48) · RN exp.: 0.55 + R0.974(2.39 − 0.55) · Aide exp.: 2.45 + R0.236(3.6 − 2.45)
